title: Why this sphere exists
summary: A sphere is how a large, hard-to-memorise body of working knowledge is reduced to the smallest set a fresh LLM can consult to be correct in a niche on demand. Authoring a good one is itself a craft with real failure modes: inventing content with no grounding, forcing everything into weak rules, shipping code instead of lessons, forgetting the doctrine alongside the technique, and never qualifying the artifact. This sphere records the method behind the sibling spheres (accounting-rigour, llm-containment, python-best-practices, bash-best-practices) as repeatable, grounded guidance.
evidence_note: PLABEL: grounded-in-authoring. These lessons come from building the spheres named above against real systems (bashqueues 0.18.139 and the ooRexx/money codebases) and qualifying them with the Gopher engine. Where a claim is engine behaviour, it cites the engine; where it is craft, it reflects what those builds did.
invariants: A sphere encodes decisions and authoritative continuation facts; it does not reproduce the whole source tree it documents.
Grounded, durable lessons beat a broad survey of a domain.
A good sphere lets a forgetful model be locally correct instead of fed yet more raw repository context.
Build small, grounded, and version it; grow edges only from real need.
